profile.headline: Software Engineer at Solidigm in Rancho Cordova, CA
profile.summary: Graduate from Sacramento State with bachelor's of Science in Computer Science, currently working at Intel in Folsom, CA as a Firmware Development Egineer

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.locationName: Rancho Cordova, California, United States · Hybrid
positions.description:
Leveraged simulation techniques in early firmware development to validate functionality and test on new unproven hardware. This allowed for bug identification and corrections before physical hardware availability, ensuring reliable results when moving to hardware. In addition, able to simulate and cover special IP related scenarios, ensuring feature requirements met before hardware availability.

Other tasks include porting and developing test for new firmware/testing environment. Ensuring firmware continued to follow previous design requirements and scope new or adjust old requirements as features evolve and hardware limitations become apparent.

Currently developing in C, C++ and Python.

positions.title: Software Developement Engineer
positions.description: I am accountable for developing and overseeing test plan to exercise different failing points in firmware, ensuring that the reliability and quality of the firmware meets the expected requirements. I work closely with my team in all testing aspects from test code to firmware, and developers to the architects, reducing and solving failures and gaps as quickly as possible.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Development and implementation of test software to validate firmware on platforms to ensure that all peaces work well with other peaces before the final product is released to the customer. 
Work with custom software designed to automate different types of tests that ensure that stress tests, communication channels, and other firmware all function as expected with little to no bugs as possible. Ensure that automation tests run efficiently and effectively cover correctly the specific aspects of firmware ensuring that no gaps are present. 
Other task involve maintaining automation of software/tests, providing support for running tests across multiple platforms/operating systems and ensuring that tests are completed by deadlines.

projects.title: Computer Game Architecture and Implementation
projects.description: In Spring 2014, similar to Object-Oriented Computer Graphics Programming (CSc 133) project, the course was centered around creating a game. However, the course was centered on using a graphics engine that was created by the school previous masters program. The engine was Java based and used concepts from Advance Computer Graphics to render objects in 3D space. The goal of the project was to first work by your self to understand how to use the engine, then work with a partner to create a fully working game with an objective and purpose.

projects.title: Intelligent Systems (CSc 180), Modified Chess Competition
projects.description: In Spring 2014, this project revolved around creating an intelligent program that could play against another computer in a competition of modified chess where we could see if whose program could make the best moves and win. The language was open, and each program had to make a choice within 5 seconds or they would be DQ. This project utilized decision trees, min-max, historical tables, etc.
